newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ debt ends firmer on higher TWI, U.S. Treasuries.
newsitem.headline: NZ debt ends firmer on higher TWI, U.S. Treasuries.

text.p: Figures in brackets compare against previous day's close
New Zealand debt markets closed firmer on Tuesday, the short end rallying on a higher Trade-Weighted Index compared with Friday's close and bonds taking heart from stronger U.S. Treasuries.
But dealers said prices had been marked up early in the session and the remainder of the day had seen little action.

The 90-day bank bill rate closed 11 points lower at 6.96 percent in response to the higher TWI. Dealers said a rate set this morning had temporarily pushed the 90-day rate down to 6.91 percent before it returned to a more natural position.
"It seems fairly steady around these sort of levels and the TWI has just steadied itself a bit as well," said a money market trader. "There is a bid tone, but it's dependent on the TWI."
In the bond market, yields were about 10 basis points lower in line with higher U.S Treasury prices.
"We'd had reasonable strength in the States, and that was enough to take it through," said a dealer. "If they continue to rally, we're more likey to be bought than sold."
